So, and when we had a chance to sit and talk, man, how he saw the team was exactly how I saw it. AG, you spent a week with him, basically. Say it again. You just spent a week together flying around the country. >> Well, that was that's that's like that's even But like I'm wondering like when you guys are together for that long a period of time, is it all ball talk? Do you guys have any fun or >> No, no, yeah, yeah, we do stuff outside of it. I mean, some when we were on the plane, his foot hit my foot. I'm like, whoa. >> So, so that was the argument we got into. But, um, no, man, it's it's we get away from football. Yes. You know, and and we just talk about, you know, life, kids, things like that, which again, it makes the relationship even better when you can you can get away from, you know, things that we know that's important and really talk about other things that are important, too. So, AG, you guys were so good on special teams last year. I think a lot of people were surprised to see Nick Folk leave Yeah. Are you concerned about the kicker position right now? Listen, it that's that's a position that you're always concerned about because because of the nature of how this game is. I mean, a lot of these games three points or less as far as so Man, we really have to go through that process and make sure that we find the right guy for us. Yes, it's always hard you know, losing a guy like that. Um but here I I I have the ultimate trust in Banjo, in Coach O'Day to get the right I mean, they are outstanding doing their job and find the right guys for us. And they exhaust every option to make sure we find the right guy. And I have total trust in those guys of being able to do it. You've been around this game a long time and you know it's basically a bottom line business. So, coming off three wins personally, like how much pressure do you feel to show progress this year? I might be different than than um than a lot of coaches when I guess when that question is asked because you know, you hear the narrative. I'm not you know, worried about my job I'm not. But I always put pressure on myself. I've always done it as a player. So, that's just that's just who I am. You know, to me it it's a pressure-packed business. You know, as a corner it's pressure. As a head coach it's pressure. So, it's always pressure. That never goes away. Now, when it comes to directing all that I mean, I got it. But let's I'm going to put pressure on myself every game, every year. It doesn't matter. I don't care if we won if we went to the Super Bowl. It's always pressure because now you have to try to repeat that. So, I look at it that way. You know, I don't look at it for anything other than that of it's a pressure-packed business and listen, you got to win. That's what it's about. You have used safeties a lot of different ways over the years. >> Say it again. You used safeties in a lot of different ways over the years. Yeah. In terms of Demaryius specifically Yeah. >> is versatility going to be a plus and then how much can his influence help that football team? I mean, it's it's it's the reason why he's here, you know, because of his influence. and I told him my definition of leadership is really influence and that's what he brings to the table. You can go back to New Orleans when Marcus Williams the things that he's done then going to Detroit with Kerb and BB, the things that he's done man, he knows that and he see that within the defense that we're going to run and he's excited about that. So, being able to use him at nickel, being able to use him at safety, being able to use him at dime. Those are number of just a different like spots you can put him in and watch him be successful. And then it's hard to ID him when you're able to do that as an offense. Well, how do you feel about your your wide receiver room? And well, you have Garrett obviously and AD made some catches and stuff last year, but Yeah. And so, you hear Garrett all the time and you should because he is a a a true number one receiver. Um but man, I I look forward to seeing what AD is going to do, you know, going through OTAs, going through the workout program, um understanding exactly how we go about doing things. I think it takes that summer time to be able to bond with your teammates and then getting to the season. I know we just got him like during the season, but to be able to see him go through the whole process with our guys um I really look forward to that. And then like Isaiah, I mean, obviously he's our punt returner, uh kick returner also, but seeing him in the slot and being able to do some things. So, I'm I like the way our receiver room is. I mean, obviously you're always going to try to get players um that's going to help your team. So, um but I look forward to seeing those guys work together. Is there a player that maybe is flying under our radar, but that you expect this year to take a nice leap that might surprise some people this I don't think he's flying under the radar, but I'm really looking forward to seeing what Mason does this year. He's talented. Yeah. I I I I think Mason's going to have a hell of a year. I I really do. Um cuz there are some things that we talked about. That's something I talked to his dad about, you know, if when we were in Miami uh working those guys out. Um that you're going to see him like take another step. So, I'm excited about that I'm excited about our our tackles, our blocking tackles. Seeing those guys the way they're going to operate. Um obviously I'm excited about, you know, all the guys we got in free agency. So, you see how those guys but if you if you were to ask me for one person, like Mason, like that's the guy. I think he's going to take another step. With some of these trades that our conversation at the end of the year, exit interviews that was one of the realest conversations that I've had yet for a rookie, too. And just like I tell you how I evaluate myself and he hear that. You know, when he said, "Coach, just like you said you were that, I'm evaluating myself, too. And here are some things I know I have to work on. And here are some things you need to hold me accountable for which he know I will so I can make sure I take the next step. Um and again, that was a real conversation and he was very adamant about what the things that he want to get better at. So, again, another player with a chip on his shoulder. You know, and I feel like um he understands what he got to get better at and how he's going to go about doing it. Another Muji question, but >> Yep. I I feel like a lot of general managers in the league they they everyone publicizes draft picks, but like it's like don't trade the pick. Don't trade the pick. It's because of the unknown instead of using them to acquire players that are known. It seems like Darren is a bit more open to the idea of like the sixth, why don't we Yeah, it's a lottery ticket in a way, but why don't we go get the player that we know exactly what he can be and that can help our team now. Is that like a a breath of fresh air? Cuz I don't I don't feel like that's a a sentiment shared by many around the Yeah, I I I I I I think I understand the question and I think it goes back to what um what we were saying what I was saying before is man, we love the player let's go get him. If we love the player, let's go get him. And I think he does a really good job number one of me and him communicating on like how should we go about doing this? Um and I think he said this before, man, his his his his phone he's going to answer the phone, you know. Um which I love that, you know, cuz you never know. You never know. Um man, the the the draft day is is I love that day. I really do cuz you never know what's going to happen. You hear all these guys that's going to get drafted in these certain spots and it's never that. >> You know, so to me that's the exciting part of it and I love every part of it. Hell, I was a part of it when I came out. Shoot, I thought I was going to be the sixth pick and I I ended up going 12, so that's how it happened. Last one here, guys. All right, let me make it a good one then. Oh. >> Here comes the heavy hitter. You spoke You're going to take his spot? Yeah, yeah. You spoke uh when you got hired, you know, got unfinished business with the Jets. And the Denver game and your memories. That's big picture. I know you're you're you're focused on day-to-day what you're doing. But how often do you reflect on like I want to end this playoff drought. I want to get this team to the mountaintop. How like how often does that come into your mind? Every day. Every day. there's a couple things I think about on a daily basis. Number one, I think about the players every day. And I think about like and I really really think about this. Now, this is not just coach speak of like how do I utilize every player that we have on this roster to help us be successful. And then two, what are the things that I have to do to make sure that man, we get over that hump because I've been a part of it and there's no better feeling in the world than Okay, so we were down trying for a number years and then we finally get over that hump. And now we're moving. But then again, so now how do we keep that sustainable for years to come? Uh I want to leave a legacy. I do. You know, when I'm when I'm gone I mean, I'm I'm I'm I'm looking at this team being a team that that consistently puts themselves in a in a place to win. And but every day, you know, it's not it's not a day, it's not an hour, it's not a minute that I don't think about and I look forward to trying to make that happen. I really do.

title: Jets HC Aaron Glenn & GM Darren Mougey Exclusive Interview: QB Position, Draft Capital & More
text: We'll beat anybody in the world, and I think we're going to win next Sunday. >> [screaming] >> Can't wait. Hey G, what's this past week been like for you because you guys are hard at it as far as scouting the college prospects before the NFL draft, and now you're here in Phoenix at the annual league meetings. >> Yeah, well, it's it's always good to to get a chance to be around these other head coaches, have conversation with those guys. Really get a chance to get the nuances of the league and some of the things that we're trying to improve on as a league and just over education, you know, for all of us, you know, so it's it's been good. It's still a process to to to get through everything, get through all the meetings, but to get a chance to be around these owners, get a chance to be around these other head coaches, it's been a good experience. >> Where do you think the league is going? I'll tell you what, when you when you look at the things when it when you talk about AI, I mean, those are some very very intriguing things that we're actually moving towards. So, listen, it's something that that we can take advantage of as a coaching staff, and we're looking at every option to be able to do that. And listen, we have some of these young innovative guys on our coaching staff that have a good idea of how to educate all of us, you know, when it comes to that, and we're going to utilize that as much as we can. >> That's one thing you emphasized in Indianapolis. You really like the blend of the coaching staff that you have some seasoned veterans like yourself, and then you do have some younger guys. >> Yeah, and again, that was intentional. And everything about what we're doing and what we're going to do is is going to be process oriented. And I really took some time to really dig deeper into what that means, and a lot of times you have this vision of of where you want to go, all right? But being process oriented means you're very detailed on the steps that you're going to take to be able to get to that vision. And that's with the coaching staff, that's with building our team, that's with basically anything that we're doing. You know, we want to be a process and don't miss miss many steps. And I think sometimes people think that you elongate a lot of things that you're doing, but you're really that's just trying to make sure you hit all those steps. You spoke about options before. When you guys approach this off season, you look at the global landscape of the quarterback position, why do you end up with Geno, and what do you think about him coming back to the green and white for second time? Yeah, that was a um um something that me, Mo Woods, and everybody that was involved wanted to make sure we took our time. It's like, what guy actually fits the Jets? And when you look at Geno, he's a guy that has a chip on the shoulder. He's a guy that's highly competitive. He's a guy that that really really loves football. He's a guy He's a guy that has learned from some of his mistakes as a young player and now want to make sure that he understands that, man, he's a key key component of that locker room and getting everybody on the same page. So, when you look at those things, those things are some of the cultural things that we want to have on this team. And man, there's nothing better than having a guy with a chip on the shoulder ready to go out there and play. So, I look forward to him coming out, being there for the first day of our phase one, working out with the players, getting a chance to get cohesive with all the players, and understanding exactly what we're trying to do on offense. Do you like that setup with him, Frank Reich, you signed Bill Musgrave to head your quarterbacks? As far as that room is concerned, then overall offensively, you bring back four of your top five offensive line starters. You signed Dalton Parham in free agency. You got all your backs back. We know you put the tag on Breece Hall. Yes. And Garrett Wilson leading your receivers, but like AD Mitchell is another year, you know, with those guys. So, I mean, you just hit it like really like on the head when it comes to our offense. Everything with us always starts in the trenches. That's O-line and D-line. And to be able to have four of the five starters back, be able to pick up a guy like Parham, and then put Geno behind something like that along with Frank Musgrave, and let's not to mention Seth Seth and Ryan. He's another guy, young guy. Um very innovative that's going to come with some really good ideas. So, I'm excited about what we have on offense, and not to mention that we're going to continue to build upon that. It's exciting for us. Do you think Geno can help unlock some things down the field because if you look at him throughout his career, he's made defensive coordinators like yourself back in the day, and you'll be calling plays this year. Defend every blade of grass. Well, >> [clears throat] >> I just remember my time defending him, and you guys can go back and look at, you know, how those games went playing him. And they were tough, and he has an electric arm. He's extremely smart, and the thing that I told him that I just I clearly saw from playing against him is just how he's matured over his years and being able to just take command of the offense when it comes to protections, when it comes to getting in and out of plays, and putting us in the right play. All right, I think that's going to be a huge thing that Frank's going to be able to take advantage of, a guy that has seen it before, that knows how to get the offense in the right play, and we want to take advantage of that as much as possible. >> Have you thought about what the play-action game could look like? Because we're talking about you want to build in the trenches. >> Yeah. You look Frank look at Frank's history. Whenever he's been calling plays, that's Hey, that is an emphasis, and you we know what you want to do. You want to run the football. Yeah, well, that has a lot to do with the guys that we have, too. We have an O-line that's aggressive, and they take great pride in the run game. And then you look at the backs that we have. Obviously, Breece is a is a is a top back, and he's going to do outstanding in this offense. Then you have BA, then you have Isaiah. So, I think we have a chance to run the ball really well. When you have a chance to run it well, that opens up your play-action game. So, Garrett, AD, Mason, all those guys, skill guys that we have, man, it's just going to open them up a lot more. What about the defensive side of the ball? Did you go into this thing thinking that I need a couple quarterbacks on that side as well because I've been saying that you guys got three quarterbacks this off season. One is Geno on the offensive side. Two is Demario, and the third one back there in the secondary is Quincy Williams. >> Yeah, well, you know what? That was a plan from the very beginning, not just on the defensive side, but just on the whole team of trying to um trying to get an influx of these veteran guys to be a part of what we're building. I think we had the second youngest team in the league last year. And listen, those guys are bought in. When I say they're they're all bought in, so now we get some of these veteran guys that's been there, done that, know how to do it, and can try to keep us sustainable, you know, from what we're doing. And that's what those guys have done, you know, so when it comes to the defense in particular, man, we have some salty guys. And I mean, that's how you want to play defense. Um but I love everything about what we're doing. And again, we're going to continue to try to build. Did you go in the off season saying, "Hey, we got to get bigger on that side of the ball"? Um because I see some trademarks when you look at Parcells back in the day and and the way he ran the thing. Yeah. Physical, no doubt about it. You want every defense to be physical. I know that. But but just when you look at the size dimension now. Well, it's a it's a big man's game. I think we all know that. >> [snorts] >> Um and more or less, just how we want to play defense, the things that we want to do. I think all those things take part in the type of players that you want to make sure you put on your team. Sweat is a guy that can control the middle, and and we wanted that. If you look at what he's done over over the time he's been in the league, he's been pretty good at run defense, and he's been sneaky when it comes to being able to push the pocket, you know, as a pass rusher. But all the other guys, David Onyemata, who I know very well, I mean, not only is he a good run defender, but he is a sneaky good pass rusher, also. And that just goes to everybody you know, that we brought in. Kingsley Enagbare, obviously Demario, the things that they can do defensively actually fit what we're trying to do schematically. So, that's that's always a plus when you can get the guys that fit what you're trying to do schematically. Schematically, do you have more options now because you mentioned like Sweat before. I know people are saying, "Well, he wants to run a 3-4." And I say, "Well, he can run a 3-4, but you know, that's a number of plays per game because you're going to be changing this up." Yeah, I think it's funny when you hear that. Listen, we're going to be whatever we have to be to be successful. And the thing is, I think in this day and age um you know, you could say 3-4, you could say 4-3. I mean, listen, it's you know, teams are so multiple nowadays that meant to be able to jump in and out of different fronts means is always advantageous you know, to a defense because you don't want to just sit in one spot and let the offense know exactly where guys are going to be. What's your selling point with guys because to a man, you talked to Demario. Obviously played with you before. He knows what you're all about, but he wanted to come here. Mecca said he jumps on the phone with you, and there's an instant connection there. So, when you tell guys, "Hey, man, I want you to join this crew." I mean, why do you have the instant buy-in? Um well, it's it's [clears throat] it's a lot more than than that. Um I think players know that I don't BS them. And um I know exactly, you know, where we are, and I know exactly that we didn't have the year that we wanted to have. Um and when you explain that to them and and don't try to sell them on anything, but just give them, "Listen, this is the vision. This is where we're trying to go. All right? And this is where I know we can go with you being a part of that. >> Um this is how we go about practice. This is what I believe in. These are the type of players that that we want. We want guys that really love football. How much do you really love it? Yeah. You know, and I think I get passionate when I get a chance to talk about that. And I think they feel that. And I think um a lot of times when you authentic about how you want to do things, when you are authentic about who you are as a coach, I think a lot of times that resonates with players really, really well and they want to be a part of that. How much does it help you not only on the field, but off the field, inside the locker room, in the meeting room, when you got guys like Onyemata, Yeah. >> DeMario, Yeah. >> and and Minkah. Well, those um I will I will say those guys real quick cuz those guys been with me and they know exactly what I'm about, you know? And when you have guys, when you bring another guy like Minkah, who um just his history of what he's done in this league speaks for itself. Um and now the young guys have someone to point to and say, "Man, this is what I want to be like and this is how I want to do it." Okay, you have no excuse now. So, all you got to do is just jump in with them, you know, cuz I know what those guys are going to do. So, now they got to bring those other guys. And those guys have have a responsibility, too. And they know that. And and I've stressed it with those guys. And I think they they understand they like that part of it. Um it's not just about you, it's about bringing everybody else along with you. And those young guys have to buy into that. Not too far away from the draft. We got to let you get out of here, but can you speak about the options you guys have as far as the draft capital is concerned? And you went on the ground, like we mentioned at the top. You've been all over the place. Yeah. Cross-country tour. What is What's it been like? >> listen, um I love every part of it. Um I mean, Moosh has done an outstanding job, him and his staff, as far as uh setting the table of these are some guys, here's the information behind these guys. Now, let's take a look and see which one fits us best. And to have two first-round picks, to have two second-round picks, to mean to have the picks that we have at the middle and at towards the end of the draft, that really sets your team. That really sets your team. That first-round picks, that those are the easy ones. It's the ones from the third, fourth, fifth, or sixth round, those are the ones that really set your team up for success. And with our coaches having to develop those guys, so I'm excited about it. Um I love having those later picks, also, cuz it gives you a chance to um truly pick some guys that they might not have all the traits that you have, but they have something in them that you know that you can develop to make them a key part of your team. So, I'm I'm excited about that part. Great seeing you as always. Appreciate your time. No doubt. Appreciate you. Darren, this is a bit of a homecoming for you, right? You grew up down the street. It is. Just grew up about 12 minutes up the street, so it feels good to be back. I love the heat. I miss the heat. Um got in Saturday night, got a chance to stop by my mom's house, see my mom and some family, so that was nice. How is she doing? She's doing great. She's doing great. But I have a brother and sister here still in town, didn't get to see them, but I got got a chance to see my mom and feels good to be back. I've asked you this before, but you were a star high school quarterback. So, do you remember those days? >> Oh, yeah, I remember those days. Those are the It feels like a lifetime ago, but I do remember those days. Those were good days. Um well-traveled of late, right? Yeah. >> You were all over the place, cross-country, last week. We were last week. It was great to get out. We we started down in Miami, were there, and then we jumped up, Notre Dame pro day, went over to Ohio State, went over to Texas Tech, and then finished at Alabama, working out Ty Simpson. It was a great week. Um Good up >> opportunity for me to get out there and get some exposure to these some of these players I hadn't seen, see them up close and personal, work out, get to spend some time with them, have some dinner, get to know them a little more on a personal level, um which was great. And also, you know, just traveling that whole week with AG, Frank, Billy Musgrave came with us because we got some exposure to some quarterbacks, and just being around them for the week is so so productive on some level, just having football conversations all the time and about the team, so it was great. It was It was a It was a long week, but it flew by. And now we're here, and I flew here Saturday and excited to get back to Jersey at the end of this week and jump right into the draft process. Uh do you really like that room now when you're talking about Reich and all the experiences he has? And speaking of experience, Bill Musgrave. And then we're going to get to the quarterback position. You added a veteran there in Geno Smith. Yeah. I do. I like the room. And just on on the Frank and Billy piece, like I said, it's been great talking quarterback play with them and offensive play this past week. And Frank's really in He's into the draft process. I mean, he's texting me all the time. He He's been great just getting to know those guys. And yeah, like you mentioned, we have Geno in the room, an experienced player who's been through a lot in this league, played at a high level, can still throw the heck out of the ball, can make all the throws, tough. So, really excited to get Geno back, see him um kind of get on the field in these OTAs and lead the team. What are those conversations like when you're talking with Frank and Bill because you all three played the position? Yeah, it No, they're great. They're awesome cuz we all kind of have perspectives and different experiences and talk about it. So, they're a lot of fun. Obviously, AG's in that, too, and he sees it through a different lens. And they're they're fun conversations. We can go around and round. Why was Geno the right fit for you guys right now? He was, you know, just just his experiences and what was available and him being able He can still make all throws. Always had a great arm, you know? And and we we were able to have some conversations with him. Obviously, the Raiders granted us permission, had some good conversations with Geno. It felt like it was a really good fit for for all parties. So, excited to get him back. Uh what do you make of his past 4 years? Obviously, things didn't work out with the Raiders last year, overall. But that 3-year one 3-year run with Seattle. Uh why did he have a a career resurgence? Yeah, exactly. He He played really good ball, you know, those those years in Seattle. And then obviously last year had a little bit of a down year. And there's a lot of things that go into that, you know? But we feel really good about where he's at physically and excited to get get to work with him, put some pieces around him, and help him out. Yeah, one thing I was asking AG about was do you like that, hey, we have the ability to be two-dimensional on offense now? When you're looking at Geno's numbers, I mean, one thing that he's always done is got a high completion accuracy. And those 4 years, you average them, he's nearly 3,800 yards per year. I know he's talked publicly about the fact that he wants to get the turnovers down, as well. Yeah. Yeah, and that's that's a group effort, you know? That's that's a collaborative effort that we that we got to, you know, be on the same page with the with the players and make sure he's protected up. It all starts really up front. Make sure he's protected up front, you got a good run game, you can build it all off that, and and be multi-dimensional, like you said. Offensively, you added a piece up front in Dalton Parham. What did you like about Dalton? Dalton was, you know, obviously with the departure of of Simpson, we had a hole there at left guard. Dalton was a guy we targeted and and had our eye on. A guy that's young, has played a lot of football. He's played left guard, he's played center, he's played right guard. So, he's got versatility, smart. I feel really good about adding him to the group, you know, a group where four of the five are returning. And we brought back Max Mitchell. We brought back Chuks. We brought back Xavier Newman. So, keeping continuity in that room, we we believe will help the room. And Steve Heiden's coming back. And I look forward to watching that group take the next step and continue to get better. We can lean on that group. We're going to see what happens over the next few weeks, but you talked about a little bit before that you like the receiver position with Garrett leading the way. Yeah. Getting Garrett back healthy this year will obviously be huge. And we'll we'll make the focal point Garrett there in the receiver room. But I'm I'm I'm excited to see AD Mitchell take the next step, Isaiah Williams, uh Aryan, those guys continue to grow and develop and take the next step. But no different than any position on the field. We'll always look, you know, at the wide receiver market, whether it's via trade, on the street, the draft, and want to add guys that we think they can help or improve our depth. What about the defensive outlook as you enter the off-season? When you and AG got together, what was the plan? How did you want to attack this thing? Well, generally speaking, going into the off-season, you know, we looked at the roster. We had one of the younger rosters in the NFL. So, we we we we were going to have an emphasis. We wanted to inject some veteran experience and leadership onto the team as a whole. And then on defense, finding certain pieces that were going to fit the hole as well and add some some experienced players like David Onyemata up front, Double D at linebacker, Minkah Fitzpatrick in the in the secondary. Then two edge players, you know, with Efe Obada and Ossai. You know, feel really good about those pieces we added and excited about those see those guys playing this defense. What do you think DeMario and Minkah, and you mentioned DO, as well. What can they add to the culture here? Just that. They can bring that veteran leadership, you know, that experience, help build the culture, the toughness, the grittiness, the professionalism, all those things, cuz that's what they've been their whole careers and have displayed that. So, excited to see that. So, now looking ahead, you got number two overall, 16 in the first round. You got that top pick in round two. You got four picks in the top 44. What happens now at this point when you get back to Jersey as far as the draft board is concerned? >> Yeah, excited about those opportunities ahead of us. And you know, what happens now is we get back later in the week, and I'll have meetings starting Thursday, Friday, and then all the scouts come in Sunday, and then that Monday we'll pick it up, and we'll be in draft meetings for the, you know, 2 3 weeks leading up to the draft, have the coaches in there, very collaborative, detailed, thorough process as we build the board. And and I'm looking forward to it. It's a time of year I I I really enjoy. I love it. So, I I look forward to it. Uh your philosophy on trading overall. You've made a number major deals here, including in this off-season, Germaine Johnson sent to the Titans and bringing in Davondre Sweat back. Yeah, just in terms of trade. That's just another mechanism to build the the team and the roster. Um, but in terms of Germaine, just we were forecasting kind of the the edge market in free agency in the draft and felt like we could add some pieces there. He was in the last year of the fifth year. Um, it's hard to find DTs. Davondre was a piece and a and a type we were really looking to add. So, glad it worked out for all parties there. title: ‘It really is about the players’: Owner Carrie Walton Penner shares benefits of new training center
text: Sitting down at the NFL annual meeting with owner Carrie Walton Penner. Carrie, we are about 2 months removed from an AFC Championship game appearance. A lot of exciting initiatives coming up. How would you characterize the momentum of the organization heading into 2026? The momentum is really exciting. Not only for the Broncos, but for our fans across Broncos country. Our players are coming back in a few short weeks. Off the field, it's amazing to watch the momentum grow as we get ready to move into our new training facility. And uh we'll be doing that in just a couple of months. And then, you know, looking at and thinking about a new stadium. And a lot of the work with neighborhood organizations and city council members, the mayor, really all of our partners in thinking about and looking at our preferred site in Burnham Yard and getting ready for uh you know, that momentum to continue. Absolutely. Uh speaking about moving across the field in just a few months to the new Broncos Park powered by Common Spirit. What's it been like to see the progress there? And what do you think the biggest benefit for the organization is in moving into the new training center? Well, it's been exciting to watch it across the field um as it has, you know, from groundbreaking until uh to today. And so, uh we're just now getting ready to put some final touches on over the next couple months and then get ready to move across. You know, a couple of things in terms of the great benefit that this will bring. Part of it is we're staying in our home and we're just moving across field. So, um so I think that the energy that comes with that is fantastic. We as an organization, we will be bringing most of the folks from the stadium who work up there into the building. And so, having the organization all together will make a huge difference in terms of having one organization, one team that really are um all together and located um in our new facility. And then for players, it really is all about the players. And from ground zero, first floor, it is the players floor. And they have the heart of that is their locker room. It's a much uh bigger and enhanced locker room. But all around them, we we designed it with the idea that we want our players taking as few steps as possible to get everything that they need and have access to everything they need. And uh really conserve their energy for getting things done on the field. As we continue to move toward Burnham Yard as the preferred site for a new stadium, how vital has the local community feedback been to the start of this process? Yeah, well, it's been fantastic and it's been really exciting. Part of it's been really exciting to hear and learn about the history of Burnham Yard. But we're still in listening mode right now, doing a lot of work with um community members, um city council, the mayor's office. The governor's been very a great partner and very supportive. The momentum is certainly there and and we're excited to partner across the community um to make this an incredible year-round opportunity for Denver and for the organization. Carrie, obviously the Broncos are not alone in this stadium project. A lot of other stakeholders. Can you tell me a little bit more about what this process is like with all of those stakeholders in the community? Yes. Well, so we have a number of different processes in place and and kind of running simultaneously to each other. We really are getting to a point where we're um all of these partnerships and the conversations we and we need to just keep making the timelines. But it'll be an incredible project and it's been a great thing to work on. Great to partner with so many different organizations and city council and other offices across across the city and the state. You know, it takes all of us. And Damani and Tim have been doing an amazing job for for us in being out there and really listening to community members and organizations and and driving this forward. But the timeline is aggressive and so we're we're looking forward to getting a little bit uh little bit more momentum there, too. We just passed the 1-year anniversary of the all-in-all covered unprecedented initiative. We just aired a 9 News special on Saturday. As you look back on the past year and the impact of the program, what makes you most proud? 99% of high schools across Colorado and programs have signed on to this. We have distributed almost 4,000 helmets over the last year. So, that's been really exciting. Um and just to see that that this is something that's creating incredible momentum across Colorado is fantastic. Absolutely. I know you're involved in several different committees. What does this week down here at the annual meeting look like for you? For the last few years, I've been on the NFL Foundation board. And then um the diversity committee. So, I've been doing those for a few years. And this year I added the player health and safety. All three of those really are in alignment with what my background is and and my engagement with the team as well in different areas. So, you know, so it's great to see a lot of the different improvements, some of the rules that we will be listening to tomorrow, the rule recommendations and changes for players on the field. And you know, as the NFL continues to really focus on how do we strengthen the game and how do we make sure the game is as safe as possible, it's exciting to be a part of that. Absolutely. Well, Carrie, we appreciate you spending some time with us. Thank you and Great. Thank you. Great to be here.
