title: Liam Coen Checks in From NFL Owners' Meetings | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: Welcome into Jags AM. Brian Sexton [music] along with John Oehser here on a Tuesday morning and we're changing things up a little bit. Not just a different host today, but we're starting with the head coach of the Jaguars, Liam Cohen, who joins us from the NFL's owners meetings in Phoenix, Arizona. The owners [music] meetings began on Sunday evening. There's lots to talk about and of course we'll get to those things, but first we bring in the head coach. Coach, how are you? Great, Brian. Appreciate it, man. Thanks for having me on. Thank you for making time for us this morning. Hey, just generally, how's the pace of your second off season? Or actually, your first off season, your second spring with the Jaguars. How different is it for you this year than it was last year when you put your feet on the ground? Yeah, it's a lot different, I'll say. Um this is probably the the first off season Ashley and I and the and the family has had in in roughly 5 to 6 years. So, uh to have a little bit of a schedule, a routine, some stability that involves pouring into football when when at the office and and with the coaching staff, but also having an opportunity to be a be a husband, be a father, um and and be able to spend some time with the family at nights is is definitely nice to have, to have some consistency throughout an off season without moving and restarting and and picking up and uh being a part from your family. Um it's been great to have so far. Coach, we talked a little bit earlier this off season about the whole idea of coming back and but you would think that you have a longer off season cuz you're here, but you don't really look at it that way. You look at it more like, "Hey, we're losing a week or two because of the rules that you can't get with these guys because you're not a new coach anymore." Uh talk about your pace of the off season, what you're trying to get done. Yeah, it's definitely um you know, you feel a little bit of a sense of of urgency. I mean, there there's there's no question in my mind that's been the challenge to the coaching staff, to our our department staffs uh at the building. The message has been um and and when the players get in in in here, the message will be uh how do we improve? How do we get better with less time together? Flat out. Less time together as a staff, less time together um once the players get in here and and and so our time on task, our intentionality has to be uh better than ever. And and that's the challenge that I have for everybody and myself included. So, um that's something that you work through and and the way that you schedule out your off season program and plan and uh the amount of repetition, the amount of time on each drill and uh where you're allocating your time. And and and so those are all the things that we've been looking at and uh certainly excited to get these players back in the building here soon so we can really start football. You know, momentum never carries over from one season to the next. Though most observers, fans also, kind of think, "Well, we were 13 and four." How do you change that mindset? Or do you have to? Do these guys understand that the boulder's back at the bottom of the mountain, time to push again? Yeah, there's there's nothing that we're defending. Uh we're attacking everything that we're doing. Um that's the mindset and mentality. We we could you know, theoretically, we could get better uh as a football team and not win 13 games. Like that's something that we have to be prepared for. We have to understand um because if we live in those results of last year, uh this ain't going to be a fun process and we won't like what we see. I got to believe that. So, everything that we attack uh from this off season moving forward as we go into uh this new uh regular season here, it's all brand new. I mean, yes, there's going to be some uh ability to start uh at ground one or two and and different levels of your offense, defense, and special teams, your systems, but there's going to be new players, there's new coaches, there's new relationships and communication uh ways that we need to operate. And so, if we attack it the same way as last year and we just say, "Well, we already made that relationship. We already had that connection." Well, that's going to be a different connection on this team because every team is different. Coach, I know you spoke with our guy Ryan O'Halloran at the Times-Union yesterday. I think my favorite thing that I heard from that was you talking about not letting the stink of winning overwhelm the stink of something else. I I love the way you put that. Uh clearly that's important to you this off season. It's it sort of ties into the last question. Anything specific that you're addressing along those lines and that's your focus along those lines? Well, yeah, I said that you know, winning is a fantastic deodorant and covers up what stinks about you. It covers up what your blind spots are, what your negatives, what your um areas of improvement are. And if we can attack those areas with humility, with honesty, uh with a relentless pursuit to improve those areas, then uh we'll still continue to work on the areas in which we were good and and we need to hone in on those things, but uh look, we're always looking for better balance on offense, right? I think the running game for the first eight weeks of the season really kind of carried us offensively and allowed us to to win some of those games and then uh the pass game in the second half of the season really allowed us to go offensively. And so, we have to create a little bit more balance there. Defensively, just continuing to find that balance between rushing coverage and and and being able to play a little bit uh couple of different coverages in the back end, couple couple different front structures or pressures that you're looking at and and looking at uh you know, adding in in player acquisition throughout the draft and free agency and trades. You're you're looking all at all those things during this time. So, um and then special teams wise, we're constantly uh getting new rule proposals throughout from the league. And so, how does that affect your formations and your schemes and your fundamentals that you're coaching? So, uh it's a lot. I mean, it's never like we're just walking through a day kind of just going through the motions hoping to go home. I mean, that's not the atmosphere we we want to be in and that's not uh how we're operating. We haven't talked to you since you uh signed Chris Rodriguez. How does he help specifically in the running game? A different style than uh Travis Etienne was, but uh I know you like what he can bring in terms of down and distance, situational consistency, things along those lines. Yeah, I think like losing a player like TJ, a first round pick, the the the ability in the run and the pass and and some of the production, like that's going to be hard to match for for anybody, right? But what I always really appreciated about C-Rod, you know, when working with him in Kentucky and then following his career over the last few years has been his his, you know, rushing yards over expected and his yards after contact. I mean, I think those are the two areas that you look at where you say like, "Did you get more or about what the play was blocked for? And are are people bouncing off of you? Do you know how to make people miss?" Like how do you make people miss? There's a lot of different ways to do that. And how do you gain yards? There's a lot of different ways to skin that cat. And ultimately, uh for me and for the for the type of style of team we want to be, to be able to punch you in the mouth and and get those some of those hard yards, getting a guy like Chris to to complement that room as it stands at right now with Etienne, Laquon, and DJ and um you know, those guys. So, we're just trying to continue to add good football players in there. How about one final thought, coach? The draft is 23 days away, a little more than 3 weeks. You have 11 picks, uh four on night two of the draft, which is first night for the Jags without a first round pick. Plus, you you you have that keeping your attention. You get some guys back this year from the draft class last year who really weren't able to contribute because of injuries. Caleb Johnson stands out. Uh the second half of the season, you didn't have Travis Etienne. Just a thought on getting some of those guys back on the field in year two for them. Yeah, we're excited about some of the second year players that uh you know, whether they were able to contribute last year or not. Um but specifically, the the Caleb Johnsons, right? Jaylen McLoud didn't didn't wasn't able to play much. Uh Getting Jack Kaiser a year better, right? Getting um Travis Etienne and schedule and and the way that we look at those things on offense. Wyatt Myalms, you know, Jordan Manheim, a lot of young players that are we're continuing to see uh hopeful ascension from that can come and and either be contributors or competitors um for for playing time. Three weeks for your players back, three weeks to the draft. A lot coming up. Coach, we really appreciate you making some time on a busy Tuesday morning in Arizona. I appreciate it, guys. Thanks for having me on. Have a great day. That's the head coach of the Jaguars coming off a 13 and four season. And as he famously has said, trying to wipe off the stink of wins and making sure his team is ready to go out and play their best football in the fall of 2026. When we come back, a little normalcy for you. We have [music] big things next on Jags AM.

title: Everything It Takes To Prepare For NFL Free Agency
text: Come on. >> We have the LA photos. >> Every equipment size. >> What's up, Bolt fam? >> Signed, done. >> Just put the pen to the paper. >> Gratefully part of the Bolt fam. Ready to get to work. >> We are closing in on free agency. Here we go. When we go through free agency, we get a list of names of players that the coaches and scouts want to see. We will make an all plays and the key plays cut up for them. I bring this in. We'll name it alphabetically so it sorts in the right order. put in that folder for that specific position so the coaches know where to go and immediately are able to access that video. >> Essentially, you always got to start with the flight in. So, my itineraries are always going to look like, okay, here's the guy. He's arriving at, let's say, 8:30 at night on a Sunday. We're probably going to bring him into the facility on Monday. And then with every single player that we bring in, I make sure we have a host for him. So, I always have a go-to person that's always there for him. We're going to start with some doctor's appointments in the morning and then he's going to come back to the facility. He's going to meet his coaches. >> Uh, one thing that we always do for free agency is wait for the players to arrive so we can capture their first moments walking into the pool and then also saying their name on the big screen behind us. >> He's going to go through kind of that lap of, you know, meeting with your position coach. You're going to meet with your coordinator and then they meet with coach Harbaugh. We usually walk them around the building, show them around, whether it be the weight room so they can meet Ben Herbert who's awesome. They can meet Sal and Marco down in athletic training. And of course, got to go see equipment as well. >> So, when we sign a new player for free agency, the uh previous team they were on, their equipment staff will send us kind of a sheet like this. And this basically gives us every equipment sizing related to them. So, just to get them started, we'll kind of give them some workout gear, head to toe, shirts, shorts, uh, training pants, socks, slide, shoes, all that kind of basic stuff. So, we'll just kind of fill him in this empty locker. Put his laundry loop on the hook. Then we'll have a full zip hoodie, couple long sleeves, couple short sleeves, sweatpants, and then some training pants and some extra hangers. Some shoes. So, we'll put those in the the pull out drawer. So, we got his training shoes, shower slides, got some socks, compression shorts, and then practice shorts. We just got to lay it out so he has a feel for everything. That's kind of the the general spread for everything we get the free agents. >> They'll go sign uh then we go do some really fun media. So every agent comes in, they sign their contract, we do a photo with them just to kind of start their Chargers journey or when they resign like Josh Harris today, we do it just so through the years we can see their progression. This is our podcast table which you if you've ever watched Chargers weekly, you see prominently. It's also a giant reflective surface though, so we turn it sideways. That way we can get a reflection on the board and make a cool looking photo. Let me turn over that one. So, for each one, we'll tether the camera into the laptop, bring it right into Lightroom. That way, we can get it edited up real quick, crop it, send it out to social so they can get it posted for you. We do different tiny mics. We kind of like pick at their interests and pull out different things that we think that they might like to do so that we play into their personality a little bit. And we shoot several things with them so that we can kind of bank those for the off season. We capture their arrivals, selfie video to the fans, and just kind of get a real glimpse into like what goes on in their first day. >> Once photos finished with their contract signing photos and social's done their thing, we'll go ahead and move this desk out of the way. It's on wheels, so it makes it easy. So, we have this hype set behind us. So, when we bring in new players, we want to shoot some hero images, hero shots to use in our highlights and future use. We have this crazy motion graphic showing all of our brand colors and logos. And while we're shooting, we have this nifty little monitor here which connects to our camera. While the camera op is getting shots, we can have a director looking through our monitor here and directing to get the shots that we need. Typically we have two cameras and we are shooting simultaneously so that we cut them together in a dynamic way for our highlights. >> After the free agents finish with their photos, social the hype set, they come over to the feature set. We try to do more of a personality based piece with the free agents so that fans can really get to know our new guys. The goal is to have a compilation piece that splices each of the guys together that came in for content. We have two cameras, we have a monitor set up, and then we have somebody producing. The player will come in, throw the mic on them real quick, they'll sit down, and we just have a stack of questions for them that they can go through. >> Myth busting, and I start crying every potential place we were going to. So, >> to start, we have three separate colors to go uh up on our socials and on our digital platforms. Uh we wanted to make sure that we had as much variety as possible. you could have multiple players get announced at a certain time. So you don't want to be posting the same graphic over and over and over again. So we did a powder background one, what we call sand, which is a white color background, and then we did our gold so that we have options for these. We have the LA photos lined up in the background to kind of give a vibe of different areas in LA. But for Resign guys, since we have so many photos of them in our jersey, I wanted to make sure that we showcase as many photos of the guys as we possibly can. >> This right here is behind the app. We're going to make a change for Denzel Perryman since we're signing him back. So once I find him, I have to change his type from unrestricted free agent to a not selected and from pending to either extended, agreed to terms, and he can move to extended, he can move to tendered, he can move to signed. That's how we set up the app part of this. >> Once we sign a player, our job is to make sure that they have a profile set up and ready to rock and roll. We just make sure that like all their information's in. We set a universal password for these guys. That way, they're kind of able to use it on their tablet and access the film super easily. After that, I go ahead and make sure I assign it to their position group. That way, their coach can kind of go ahead, put all the information in, and they can access it during meetings or at home when they're kind of going back and forth. I'll update it. It'll show up in our system, and they're ready to rock and roll. Once uh we make the profiles like on Thundercloud uh we all give them their personalized tablet. So we have this app called the Catapult ThunderCloud and we just log them in with their credentials and with this app they'll be able to see all the video and their playbook. >> Yeah. Did you see what I wrote? >> It's really great. We get to bring in families. The family is the support system behind the players for the support here. This is such a great place. It's such a great facility. It's really nice to show it off to people who get to see it for the first time. >> This is such a big collaborative effort between so many different departments. There's a lot of group chats, a lot of phone calls. Everyone's trying to stay on top of everything, keep communication clear. It's really about showing these guys how great the city of LA is and how great all the people are here. >> Got to go with five. That's the next round number we got. >> All right. Uh it's time to come fight. >> Excited for day one on the wall and everything. Let's go.

title: ESPN's Courtney Cronin Talks NFC North, Free Agency Moves, Kyler Murray & Quarterback Competition
text: We're out here at NFL owners meetings, and I am joined by ESPN's Courtney Cronin. Welcome back on our Vikings channels. We love having you. >> me. This is always something I look forward to whenever we're at the combine or we come out to owners meetings, and it's my way of connecting back with the Vikings fan base. >> I know. We We have not forgotten about you cuz we watch you on SportsCenter and do all the ESPN uh stuff. So, I know you have like a really good pulse on the league in general. But, if we could just focus on the NFC North, how do you feel like between free agency, how that played out, especially for the Bears who I know [music] you cover? I think that they lose a lot of veteran leadership, whether it's D'Onta Foreman [music] retiring, DJ Moore getting traded, Tremaine Edmunds getting released. He goes and signs with the New York Giants, and Kevin Byard leaving in free agency to go play for the New England Patriots. [music] Like, this is a team that won 11 games in the regular season last year, won its first playoff game in 15 years, and they know they've got to start over at ground zero. And that's Ben Johnson's message to not only his players, it's out there in the media. He does not want to talk about 2025 anymore. I think a lot of coaches >> Yeah. have that same sort of approach, [music] but it shows you how quickly you can get success, but how quickly you can lose it because of what we've seen, the examples of teams [music] around the NFL that that's happened to, where it feels like a pop-up one year, and you try to sustain it, and you try to make the right moves in free agency in the draft, and then the next year is a step back. So, the Bears are a team that just won the division. They're trying to avoid that regression when they finally got things off on the right foot, in the right track with Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams. So, now it's how do they do that? Because right now, after a quieter free agency, but free agency where they were still active, they brought in Kobe Bryant, they brought in Garrett Bradbury, who we all know well from his time in Minnesota. >> Um they're trying to figure out a way to sustain the success without leaning on what they did last year, but knowing that the foundation is built. >> Yeah. I mean, it just kind of feels like the NFC North is always up for grabs every single season. How do you see the Vikings staying competitive in in that division? Well, they did the right thing by bringing in competition at quarterback. We knew that they were going to do that. This was all signs pointing towards JJ McCarthy still here, but he can't be the uncontested starter going in. So, you resign a quarterback in Carson Wentz, who played some pretty important games last year in place of McCarthy. But, most importantly, you bring in Kyler Murray, who gets a chance to revitalize his career. And I think for somebody who has spoken so glowingly not only about the organization and growing up a Vikings fan, >> [music] >> but getting a chance now to work with Kevin O'Connell. He has that reputation that across the league, [music] these young quarterbacks and I I still consider Kyler, even though he signed a second contract, I still consider him a young quarterback. When you want to take that next step, but you just don't feel like you're in the right place to do it, going somewhere else and working with a coach who has shown a proven track record of doing that, I think will will yield benefits for both the team and the player. >> Okay. Well, I know that you covered the Vikings for a while. You obviously have a relationship with Executive Vice President of Football Operations, Rob Brzezinski. And And he's talking to the media more, and our fans are kind of hearing him more. I know. >> More Rob. More Rob all the time. It's always a positive thing. Um but, just for just for fans who are just starting to get to know him after you covered us for so long, how like who is he as a person, and what are you excited about him getting this chance during the draft to like really put a stamp on things? >> There is no one who knows the Minnesota Vikings better than Rob Brzezinski, the institutional knowledge of someone who has been with this team since the 1990s, and seeing all of it. Like, seeing the highs, seeing the lows, seeing how they've navigated different challenges before, seeing how they've gone after the most important position on any football team, which is the quarterback, and the lessons that they've learned along the way in doing that. I'm excited for the opportunity he's going to have here, and I'm really eager to see what the draft strategy is going to be because this is a Vikings team spent a lot of money in free agency a year ago. We know that the results didn't necessarily yield the type of success the team wishes it would have had, but you've got somebody now who has like is the pulse on the whole team. He knows everybody. I mean, the the The one thing I will say about the Minnesota Vikings that is more unique than any other team that I've covered, you have people in that personnel department who have been in the trenches with Rob for decades. That doesn't always happen where it's for the a big part of it, the bones of this staff were around for previous regimes. And now that you have somebody at the helm who is among the most well-respected people in the NFL, and we know how they feel about him in Minnesota, I think it's going to be a really good thing. I'm excited to see what the future holds for him throughout this draft process and also beyond it, too. >> I know. Beyond it, it's going to be an interesting process. Thank you so much, Courtney, for your insight. Really appreciate it. Awesome seeing you. Enjoy your rest of your time in Phoenix.

title: Rob Brzezinski Talks Vikings Free Agency Moves, Quarterback Room, Approach to 2026 NFL Draft & More
text: We are out here at the 2026 NFL owners meetings. I am joined by Vikings executive vice president of football operations Rob Brzezinski. And Rob, first of all, before we get started, this has been owners meetings number This is your This is year 34 for me. I don't remember the first year I actually came down to owners meetings, but it's been a pretty good run. It has been. How has it changed with your with your with your acting role right now? Well, I got to do some media. I mean, this is >> Oh, that is true. That is so [laughter] true. I know it's your favorite. No, no, it's not. It's been great. I mean, this time of year is always busy and there's a lot going on, you know, from a roster standpoint and and and all those things we're typically dealing with and obviously a little bit more this year, but everything is going really well so far. Well, speaking of the Vikings announced they intend to exercise Jordan Addison's fifth-year option. What's the thought process behind that move? I mean, Jordan is a really, really good young player. >> [music] >> Really, really good person. We're excited to have him. You know, it's part of the process in the CBA. >> And I think we have until May 3rd, you know, to actually make that official, but for sure, you know, we intend to do that. Yeah, I mean, you're working [music] hard behind the scenes and in all the meeting rooms as well. But you also had a busy free agency period. And when we spoke the last time, you mentioned how you wanted to be intentional. How do you think that played out to what you hoped it would be? Yeah, I think we set out to do, you know, a few things and I think we executed as we had hoped. You know, there's always curveballs and and things along the way that don't go exactly as planned, but I'm really proud of the discipline we've had and we've been talking about really trying to stack good decisions and not try to force anything and I think we feel really good about how our team is positioned for 2026, you know, and the future. Yeah, I don't I don't know if enough people have been talking about some some of your moves specifically in cornerback James Pierre. What did you guys see in him that you thought he'd be a good fit for this Viking [music] secondary? I mean, our our personnel staff, our coaching staff, they just saw traits in him >> that he's going to fit Flo's defense really, really well. And that's the the great thing with Flo is and his staff, they know exactly, you know, what they're looking for in players. And then there's alignment with the you know, with our scouting staff and and able to to hunt for those guys and and find a guy like James that we're really excited to be able to add. How do you feel like you guys executed on your vision for a more competitive quarterback room? >> I don't think we could be any happier with our quarterback room. I mean, to bring in a talent like Kyler Murray, I don't even know. There's there's that speaks for itself. A sneaky, really exciting, you know, return for us was Carson Wentz. You know, the we think the world of him. And then, you know, J.J. McCarthy and and we got Max Brosmer in the room. So, we love the way that room looks like right now and and there's going to be some good competition and you know, it's exciting. So, we are a month away from the NFL draft. Vikings go on the clock at number 18, but you do have nine picks as of right now. How do you see that flexibility helping you throughout all the decisions you'll be making around that time? Well, there's still a ways to go in the process. There's still another 3 weeks of draft meetings and you know, information is still coming in from pro days and you know, with the college guys. And so, the answers to the test to some extent are still out there. So, we still have to continue to work through our process and get our board stacked objectively so we can make good decisions when we're on the clock. And I think if you do that, >> you got a great chance to be successful. Want to let you all know a little bit more about your draft philosophy specifically. How open are you to moves or trades? Well, I mean, it's not like I think it's an organizational philosophy, you know, and and there are some things that we've talked about internally about how we're going to navigate that. And I think number one is you got to get you want to get your picks right. And then, kind of next level is you can maneuver around the board a little bit and you know, pick up some extra capital here or there and and and we have some guardrails as far as how we want to do that, but we're focused on making sure we get our picks right. How have you seen yourself balance the best player available versus your biggest position of need when you are on the clock? I mean, I think it's the the the biggest reason why a lot of players fail in this business. And it's not just the player, it's it's it's it's complicit with the club is you force your need and for a lot of reasons it it doesn't work out and you you pass on a player of higher ability for a position of need. Puts undue pressure on the player and there's various other factors and you know, I may be may be old school. But if you get your board set right and you kind of look for the best player available, I think that's going to lead you down the right path. >> Yeah. Well, again, on a more personal note, when the Vikings go on the clock at 18 or wherever they do in the draft room, it'll be a much different feeling for you. How What do you think it's going to be like? You know what? Once you get in the draft room, like the the hay is all in the barn and it's kind of this unveiling of how you think [snorts] it's going to, you know, kind of come to fruition and and and what happens and and the trail winds a little bit, but you know, for the most part, we're going to be prepared and we're going to let the draft come to us and and just excited the way everybody's working together. Everybody in our organization has been stepping up in a big way and uh we're just we're ready to go. Yeah, no extra added pressure now that, you know, you get to make the call, put the pick in. >> No, we'll make we'll go through this process together and like I said, I think these these selections will be pretty obvious, you know, each time we're on the clock. Love that. Thank you so much, Rob. Enjoy your rest of your time in Phoenix.

title: ESPN's Field Yates Discusses NFL Free Agency, Trades & More on Patriots Draft Countdown
text: All right, we're excited now to be joined by Field Gates from ESPN to break down the Patriots off seasonason here. A little bit of free agency, a little bit of look forward to draft. Field, thanks for taking the time here to hop on with me. >> No problem, Duce. Glad to be with you today. >> So, let's just start off with free agency. You know, the Patriots um seem like a lot of one forone moves, you know, digs out, dos in, etc. Uh just what were your impressions here of the Patriots moves through the early part of free agency? >> Yeah, well said. And you can take it a step further with moves like Draymond Jones in, Caleb, Chaon out. They play a different style of game, but still guys that you expect to be or in the case of Chaon was a starter, a very solid starter for them at that. He was especially great down the stretch and in the playoffs. Draymond Jones, you expect to be a starting edge rusher for this franchise as well based off the familiarity, the skill set, and also the money, which is always a good thing to follow during free agency. So, it feels like an off season that um I feel like there's more to be done. And that what I mean by that is it feels like the Patriots still have some cards left to play. And that's not just the draft. It's other ways other levers to pull uh to continue to improve this roster. Obviously, it's in very good shape. They made the Super Bowl this past season, but there are a couple of items on the to-do list that I think this team is going to still look to address. >> Well, one of those items, could it be AJ Brown? I mean, there's just so much talk. I mean, Patriots fans have been talking about AJ Brown forever. >> We've been doing this dance for a couple years now. It feels now they're saying maybe after June 1st. What are your thoughts on that whole potential coming to fruition finally, AJ Brown to the Patriots, is it real? Yeah, I think where I've landed with AJ Brown is that until either he comes out himself and publicly commits to wanting to be a Philadelphia Eagle for 2026 and beyond or until we get to the start of the regular season, I'm going to believe there's a real possibility that he has traded. There's just been so much speculation and so much smoke and from some of the top insiders in the game. My colleague Adam Shester has been talking about the possibility of an AJ Brown trade and certainly made it seem like that is still in play and he's referencing that the Patriots are one of the teams that still are a logical landing spot perhaps at least in my estimation the most logical landing spot for AJ after June 1st and I think probably most viewers and listeners to this program already know this but after June 1st it becomes a lot more palatable from a salary cap standpoint for Philadelphia to trade away AJ Brown. So that's a long time to have to wait. Still two and a half more months from when you and I are talking right now. But for a player of this caliber and for a deal that would most likely involve draft capital, you can wait until June 2nd to have a guy that would immediately give the Patriots their best offensive weapon for Drake May to distribute the football to. >> Just one more question for you, Phil, about the offense. I just I felt like this was a real Josh McDaniels kind of offense. You know, we see Reggie Gilliam come over from the Bills. Josh got to have his fullback. You know, you take a little bit of a chance on on Vera Tucker who's had some injuries but has a high upside. Uh it seems to me, you know, you got to get a blocking tight end there from Miami as well. Seems like they really are focused on maybe building the toughness, the physicality, short yardage was an issue for them last year. Uh and then you also bring in Dobs. How do you see that all coming together? >> Yeah, totally agree. Especially on those first three players that you referenced, kind of the identity of what they bring to the table. Reggie Gilliam, hard-nosed, excellent fullback, also great on special teams. He'll help in that regard. Julian Hill, a name that I don't know how many people knew a whole lot about Julian Hill. He's got a very interesting background prior to playing in the NFL, but to your point, he is going to help the running game as well, played in that very unique scheme in Miami where he was on the move a lot and carving out some paths for guys like Devon Achan who of course was excellent for Miami these past couple of seasons. Um, but short yardage has to be better. Uh, you know, there's always this push pull when you've got a quarterback like Drake May who can run the tush push and assume that stays in 2026 and beyond, but also a quarterback that you want to protect. And then beyond that, you've got a player in Trayvon Henderson who we know how electric Trayvon is. He was unbelievable for stretches last season, but his role decreased down the stretch and into the playoffs. He feels like the kind of guy that's at his best running between the tackles with somebody leading the way for him. He's just not going to be this gigantic power back and Raandre was great last season, especially down the stretch. It was kind of the reverse of how Trayvon's impact played out. But I think that both of those guys will benefit from having a hammered head in front of them. Jack Westover gave them good snaps last season. Jack much more of an angular blocker, the kind of guy that's a factor in the passing. Well, at least he was during college, a factor in the passing game, but not the kind of fullback that we have seen for a lot of years for the Patriots with Josh McDaniels. Most recent versions include the likes of YaKob Johnson and maybe Reggie Gilliam can give you a bit more of what Yak gave you for those years in New England. >> Oh, I love the Yak shout out, of course. Love our German Yakob Johnson. But, uh, let's get let's get in the draft a little bit at field and this is, you know, weird. We're last couple years you're talking top five picks and it's going to be one of two or three guys. Now we're back to picking at the bottom of the first round where, you know, I always like that spot a little bit because maybe something gets pushed down that you weren't really expecting. Maybe it's not a huge need, but there's a very talented player. A lot of talk about this edge class. It's still a huge need for the Patriots. Every time I look at a mock draft, I get down to that 31st spot. Who's the edge? You know, it's it's either somebody has to slip through the cracks or maybe you're reaching a little bit. Just what are your general thoughts down there at 31st overall here in this draft? Well, there's two ways in which this is trickier to forecast for the Patriots than the past couple of years where it was pick three and then pick four. And that third pick two years ago was especially easy when it was going to be a quarterback and there were three outstanding prospects at the top and you just take whoever is left over and I think the Patriots are thrilled that Drake May is the guy they got. I think frankly all three teams are thrilled with how it played out, but that's a different conversation for a different appearance here on the show. Um, this year it's more difficult, not just because of the fact that there are infinite scenarios that could take place between 1 and 30, the 30 picks that precede the Patriots, but also it's this very unique draft class. It's a draft class that's I would say breath the blue chip talent. There are a few guys, but not a lot of real difference makers. And what you find, and earlier today, I dropped my top 50 on ESPN.com, and I try to be judicious and in checking comments uh on social media when you do things like that. However, I'd imagine there are probably some people that are frustrated about certain players being too low, maybe a couple of players being uh eyebrow raising in terms of how high they are, but this is that draft class. This is very much a choose your own adventure draft class. I don't think there's tons in the way of consensus. So for the Patriots at 31, I think the needs to me would stack up in some order of continue to add add rushers. A wide receiver with the caveat that if an AJ Brown trade might get done after June 1st, it's not quite as pressing of a need. I think a number two tight end or number three tight end, I don't however you want to categorize it, a guy that can give you a little bit more than what we have seen so far from Julian Hill as a pass catcher. Uh with Hunter Henry going into the final year of his current contract. Uh those are some of the positions that come to mind for me. Uh and then continuing of course to hammer along the offensive line. I think they have their five guys if they were to play a game tomorrow. Um but I al you know they have a chance to have their five guys if they play a game tomorrow. I certainly think you know the AVT signing gives them some real versatility and upside when he is healthy. Uh but they need to continue to add depth there as we saw during the playoff and you face off against the best pass rushers, pass rushers and pass rushes as a group. Uh you got to have not just five guys you can really count on but a great protection plan and also some depth. >> Love what you're saying about the edge and the tight end groups. I mean those are two position groups at the combine. We heard Vable Elliot Wolf both mention those. I mean the tight ends totally hear what you're saying. Like I just they get younger, get a young one of these athletic guys. Matt Cla from Ohio State, one that I like. But want to talk about two other positions down there, though. And you had Caleb Lomu from Utah as a tackle, uh, taken in 31st overall in your first mock draft, which, you know, to me, I think that's a need, too. I'd also look at the safety position. You know, does one of those guys get pushed down a little bit. They just signed Kevin B. He's on a one-year deal. He's still playing at a high level. You've got Craig Woodson kind of locked in, but that could be a long position of need. Are tackle and safety maybe two darkhorse positions down there at 31st overall that you could see them consider? I try to remind consumers of my content this all the time is that like other than quarterback, everything's kind of a need for the Patriots because the NFL is a unpredictable and there's a salary cap. So players that are currently fixtures may not be fixtures for the next five or six years. So I think that offensive line just in general talked about a need. Safety could be a need as well. Well, and I think that what we realize with safeties, and this is something that has really shifted over the past couple of years, is that there's a specific type of safety that a Mike Vrabel and Zakur and Terrell Williams defense is going to prioritize and value. Right? There were guys who just a couple of years ago looked like they were going to be fixtures for the Patriots and Kyle Duggar and also the Bro Peppers and then both of them are gone. Obviously, the Jaylen Hawkins for Kevin Bard swap is one that brings tons of familiarity. It's also a one-year deal for a safety in his 30s as Kevin Byer. So, if you could find a guy that provides some of that ability to chop off explosive plays down the field like Bayern does, he's got premier ball skills. He led the NFL interceptions once again last season did Bard, but safety is probably a bigger need than maybe is currently being forecasted. Uh, and the Patriots showed last year that you can get some good players in the middle rounds of the draft. Craig Woodson was just excellent for them and a guy that was it 102nd overall I think it was for Craig. So not quite in the middle of the draft but just prior to the proverbial 50ard line of the 2025 NFL draft. >> Wilfield I know you got another mock draft coming up. Do you want to tease that at all? I don't want you to give anything away but you know this is what we live and breathe on here in the spring. >> Yeah pass catcher will be one of the themes. Actually a two round mock draft. So, a pass catcher and but that there will certainly be a note in there that this could all change if AJ Brown is eventually shipped to New England. The delicate balance that you know Elliot Wolf and Mike Vrabel are dealing with is that you know there's no way to agree to a deal that's contingent upon getting done after June 1st. Like the NFL does not allow that. You could have an agreement in principle but it can't be fully executed. So, uh, for any number of reasons, a deal that you think is done on March 19th may not be done once June 2nd rolls around. So, you almost have to go into this draft, uh, counting on receiver as a need, address it if you so desire. Keep in mind that AJ Brown could become available, but I'm sure the Patriots and Eagles have have had plenty of conversations about how realistic that could be. and we still have five weeks until the NFL draft. So, even more time for them to kind of flesh out the parameters of a potential deal. A pass catcher will be a need there for the Patriots. I would note that uh they're in that sweet spot at the back end of the first round as well that teams will call, right? It's not just teams that maybe want to get up into the back end of the first round for a quarterback. And this does feel like one of those years where we could see a team move up for Ty Simpson out of Alabama. I think he will make it into the 20s. But the other thing that I would note is teams do want that fifth year of contract control. Uh the Carolina Panthers moved up just a couple of years ago from 33 to 32 to get Xavier Legette, the wide receiver out of South Carolina. And and and it could be that they wanted the fifth year of contract control. That's the only motivation. It also could be that if you know a team is convinced that Seattle or whoever might be picking at 32 is going to take who they really want to at the top of the second round then they could be motivated to jump ahead uh and get to number 31. So tradeback is something that I think almost every team likes to do especially in a draft class like this. So wouldn't surprise me if the Patriots are proactive and finding suitors that could come up to number 31 overall just given the fact that I think the caliber of player between 31 and 37 40 is pretty similar even in a draft in which the Patriots have at least right now the third most picks of any team in the NFL. >> A lot of uncertainty when you're down there at the bottom of the first round. Makes it a little bit more exciting I think. Of course they trade out. Could be a long night, but we'll let that happen. Feel, thank you so much for taking the time and uh we'll continue to look out for your mock drafts and uh see what comes about in April. >> Thanks, dudes. Appreciate you having me on.
